about: List prices in US dollars per million tokens, one entry per model id, read by scripts/lib/prices.py. Each entry carries its five component prices, the date they were confirmed in force at the source (effective) and where they were read (source). Anthropic first-party API rates: Amazon Bedrock and Vertex AI price separately, and US-only inference (inference_geo) multiplies every component by 1.1 on Claude 4.6 and later models; OpenAI's for the models behind Codex CLI, OpenCode's for its Console (Zen) models, xAI's for Grok and Cursor's for Composer, each from that provider's own page, where a component the provider does not bill separately carries the rate it bills it at. Grok and Composer are listed under the id each harness's reading carries: the --model slug a Cursor lane passes, since Cursor CLI prints no model (grok-4.7, grok-4.6 and grok-4.5, the Grok models Cursor's page offers, and composer-2.5), and OpenCode's <provider>/<model> id for each model on xAI's Text API table (xai/grok-4.7, xai/grok-build-0.1). premium_request is GitHub's price of one Copilot premium request, beside the token prices and never summed into them. copilot_token_billing is GitHub's Copilot token billing: the US-dollar value of one AI credit and each model's rates in AI credits per million tokens, under the dotted id the Copilot CLI records (claude-sonnet-5.5, not the API's claude-sonnet-5-5); no id there is also a models id. An entry may carry a long_context block: its provider's rates for a request whose prompt is from_prompt_tokens or more, billed at them for all its tokens, dated and sourced on their own and priced under the id <model>@long-context (xAI's Long context for grok-4.7, grok-4.6 and grok-4.5). A model not listed is reported as not priced, never as free. A project adds a model or replaces one under pricing.models in sdlc-studio/.config.yaml (reference-config.md#pricing).

models.source: https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing (Cursor models table, Composer 2.5, standard speed, where https://cursor.com/docs/models redirects, read 2026-11-09)
models.note: the --model slug a Cursor lane passes and its reading carries (the Model ID on Cursor's Composer 2.5 page); the rates for usage beyond a paid plan's weekly pool. The page lists no cache-write price, so a token written to the cache is billed as input and both cache-write slots carry the input rate. Composer 2.5 (Fast), which the page makes the product default, bills $3 input, $0.50 cached input and $15 output, and a slug cannot tell it apart: a Fast session is under-priced here

premium_request.source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-billing/request-based-billing-legacy/copilot-requests (Copilot requests (legacy): additional premium requests at $0.04/request, read 2026-11-06)
premium_request.note: the legacy request-based price: since 1 June 2026 GitHub bills Copilot by tokens in AI credits, and premium requests remain the billing unit only of a Copilot Pro or Pro+ annual plan kept on request-based billing

copilot_token_billing.source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-billing/models-and-pricing (How model pricing works: 1 AI credit = $0.01 USD; Pricing tables, per 1 million tokens; read 2026-11-09)
copilot_token_billing.note: rates in AI credits per million tokens: GitHub's page prints each in US dollars beside 1 AI credit = $0.01 USD, so each rate here is the page's dollar rate divided by the credit's value, and prices.py multiplies it back. Each id is one the Copilot CLI records, from https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/cli-command-reference (Supported models, and the models of its built-in agents, read 2026-11-09). gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-luna and gpt-5.3-codex are Copilot CLI ids too, but the Codex CLI records the same ids and the models list prices them at OpenAI's rate, which is Copilot's for every component a Copilot reading carries (the CLI splits no one-hour cache write), so they are not repeated here and no id is in both. A model on the page whose Copilot CLI id GitHub's reference does not name is not listed, and reads as not priced. The page's Long context rates bill at higher rates a session total cannot tell apart, and are not used
